title: CLCON/105/2023 of VIPIN KUMAR Vs NITESH JHA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Contempt Petition No. 105 of 2023
Vipin Kumar ........Petitioner

Present:-
Mr. Dushyant Mainali, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Chief Standing Counsel for the State.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the respondent no.2.
Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, Advocate for the respondent no.3
through video conferencing.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The petitioner has brought to the notice of the
Court wilful disobedience of the Court's direction dated
20.07.2006, passed in WPMB No.353 of 2004, Souninder
Singh Hooda Vs. State of Uttaranchal and others ("the
first writ petition").
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record. Learned counsel for the respondent
no.3 appeared through video conferencing.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that in the first
writ petition, on 20.07.2006, the Court in clear term had
declared that in future, no relative (not even the husband)
of the woman Member or Chairman of the Zila Panchayat
shall be permitted to attend or participate in the meeting

2
not even in the capacity of a nominee. Despite that, in the
meeting dated 08.12.2022, the respondent no.3,
Chairman, permitted her husband to participate in the
Board meeting of Zila Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar.
The details of the meeting were published in the
newspaper. It is a wilful disobedience of the Court's
directions dated 20.07.2006, passed in the first writ
petition.
5. A response affidavit has been filed by the
respondent no.1. According to it, an enquiry has been
initiated into the matter with regard to the allegations of
participation by the husband of the respondent no.3 in
the Zila Panchayat Board Meeting. It is also the case of
the respondent no.1 that directions have been issued that
the statutory provisions of the Uttarakhand Panchayati
Raj Act, 2016, and Court's directions dated 20.07.2006,
passed in the first writ petition, should not be disobeyed
or else strict action would be initiated.
6. On behalf of the respondent no.2 also, in his
counter affidavit, it is stated that directions have been
issued so that no representative of any Member or
Chairman shall participate in any meeting.

3
7. The respondent no.3, in its response affidavit,
has stated that the contempt petition may not be initiated
after lapse of time in view of Section 20 of the Contempt
of Court Act, 1971.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that, in fact, in the first writ petition, directions
were given for future. Therefore, the respondent no.2
should have ensured that no representative, relative of
any Member could participate in the meeting. Since it was
not done in the meeting held on 08.12.2022 of the Zila
Panchayat Board, Udham Singh Nagar, it is a wilful
disobedience of Court's directions dated 20.07.2006
passed in the writ petition.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 would
submit that in the first writ petition, the respondent no.2
was not a party. Even Zila Panchayat was not a party. In
addition to it, it is submitted that it is not the duty of the
respondent no.2 to conduct the Zila Panchayat Board
meeting. Therefore, the respondent no.2 may not be held
responsible for any irregularity that might have been
committed in any such Board Meeting. He would submit
that now, in fact, in a Zila Panchayat Meeting held on
31.03.2023, it has been categorically resolved that in

4
future no relative, representative of any
Member/Chairman shall participate in the Board
Meeting.
10. On behalf of the respondent no.3, it is
submitted that the contempt petition is not maintainable
as it is time barred.
11. This is a contempt petition. What is to be seen
is as to whether any order or judgment of the Court has
been wilfully disobeyed by the contemnor. Before doing
so, a perusal of the judgment dated 20.07.2006 passed in
the first writ petition needs to be examined. In fact, it was
disputed between Souninder Singh Hooda with the State
of Uttarakhand as well as the Chairman Zila Panchayat,
Udham Singh Nagar. The factual matrix has been stated
in Paras 3 and 4, which is as hereunder:-
"3. The petitioner's case is that in the meetings of
Zila Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar, persons other
than the members of the Zila Panchayat are
permitted to participate, which is against the
express provisions of law. The petitioner, in the writ
petition, has specifically averred that one Ishwari
Prasad Gangwar, who is husband of Mrs. Sushila
Gangwar, Chairman of the Zila Panchayat,
participated in the meetings of the Zila Panchayat
held on 16.07.2003 and 20.11.2003.
4. Counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of
respondents Nos. 1 & 2. For the reasons best
known to respondent No. 3 Chairman, Zila

5
Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar, no counter
affidavit has been filed on behalf of this respondent
though the petition is pending for the last about
two years. However, during the course of hearing,
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, the learned counsel for
respondent No. 3 adopted the stand taken by
respondents Nos. 1 & 2 and the submissions
advanced by Mr. J.P. Joshi, the learned Addl. Chief
Standing Counsel for respondents Nos. 1 & 2."
12. The Court, in the judgment dated 20.07.2006,
passed in the first writ petition has taken note of various
provisions with regard to the representation in such
meetings, and in Paras 15 and 16, concluded as follows.
"15. From the above discussion, it becomes clear
that a member of the Council of the Ministers can
nominate a person as his representative to attend
the meeting of the District Planning Committee on
his behalf. The learned Addl. Chief Standing
Counsel could not point out any similar provision
in the Adhiniyam, 1961. The absence of a similar
provision in the Adhiniyam, 1961 would necessarily
mean that a representative / nominee of a minister
is not entitled to attend the meetings of the Zila
Panchayat and the other committees of the Zila
Panchayat constituted under the Adhiniyam, 1961.
16. The inevitable conclusion of the above
discussion is that in view of the Government Order
dated 10.03.1998, no relative of a women member
or office bearer, which would include the Chairman
of the Zila Panchayat also, can attend or participate
in the meetings of the Zila Panchayat."
13. It is thereafter, in Para 17 of the judgment
dated 20.07.2006, passed in the first writ petition, this
Court issued directions.

6
14. A bare perusal of the above reveals that, in
fact, in the first writ petition, the issue was intra-parties.
The grievance of the petitioner in the first writ petition
was that how could Ishwari Prasad Gangwar, husband of
Mrs. Sushila Gangwar, Chairman of the Zila Panchayat,
could participate in the meetings. The directions in Para
17 of the judgment dated 20.07.2006 were restricted to
that effect.
15. Learned counsel for the petitioner would read
the fourth word 'future' as appears in Para 17 second line
of the judgment dated 20.07.2006 passed in the first
petition.
16. This word 'future' may not be extended to each
and every contingencies that happens in the future. That
word 'future' relates to that present, which was on
20.07.2006. This future cannot come to this PRESENT.
In addition to it, admittedly, the respondents were not
party to the first writ petition.
17. Even now, a statement has been given on
behalf of the State as well as on behalf of the respondent
no.2 that instructions have been issued that in future, no

7
relative/representative of any Member/Chairman shall
participate in such meetings.
18. Having considered the facts of this case, this
Court is of the view that it is not a case of wilful
disobedience of any judgment, order or direction of this
Court passed in the first writ petition. Therefore, there is
no reason to take any further action in this contempt
petition. It stands disposed of, accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 07.07.2023
Ravi Bisht
